ca_mustang_ranch.blurb: A compact pair of small formations in the Wonderland of Rocks, in the northern part of Joshua Tree National Park and close to Brownie Girl Dome. Most of the lines are on the east-facing sides. Trad is the main event, with nine of the fifteen climbs, joined by a couple of sport routes, two top-ropes and a pair of low-grade boulder problems. Grades lean friendly: a good handful sit between 5.4 and 5.7, a few more land around 5.9 and 5.10, and only a couple reach into 5.11 and 5.12. The grainy rock turns crumbly higher up, so be careful near the tops, and think through the descent before rappelling off the west formation.

ca_el_nino_wall.blurb: A small sport-focused wall in Corte Madera, in the southern part of San Diego County. It is the first formation you meet on the hike in, set apart from the big main cliff. Thirteen of the fifteen climbs are bolted, with a couple of trad lines, and a few can also be top-roped. Difficulty runs from easy 5.5 up to the low 5.12s, but the heart of it is 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades. Most lines are a single pitch, with one two-pitch route on the wall. The top is a pleasant spot to stop for lunch.

ca_ken_black_memorial_dome.blurb: A good-sized dome in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park, just west of the park road and a short distance beyond the turn for the ranger station. Thirteen of the fifteen climbs are trad, with one sport route and one top-rope. Grades start at an easy 5.5 and top out around 5.11, with most of the climbing between 5.7 and 5.10, so it works for solid intermediates as well as newer leaders. The main face looks east, which means direct morning sun, a nice contrast to the many shaded walls elsewhere in the park. The rock quality is good and the lines are generally worth doing.

ca_parking_lot_rock_4.blurb: A small crag in the Pinnacles South group of Holcomb Valley, in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear, at roughly 7,400 feet. The climbing is short crack and face lines, ten trad and five sport. Grades start around 5.6 and cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with a single route up at 5.13, so it is better for climbers already comfortable on 5.10 than for beginners. The base is only a minute or so from where the dirt road ends, which makes it a quick stop, and the wall gets shade in the morning and late afternoon.
ca_parking_lot_rock_4.parking_note: Drive the forest road that runs alongside the fence line all the way to its end; the crag is directly beside you there.
ca_parking_lot_rock_4.approach: About a minute or less on foot from the end of the road.

ca_gold_wall.blurb: A gold and orange face at the lower left of a larger slab in Pine Creek Canyon, above Bishop in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 7,000 feet. It holds fifteen climbs, eight sport and seven trad. Difficulty runs from 5.9 to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it is a mid-grade wall rather than a place for beginners. A short, steep scramble over talus off the main trail reaches the base. Combine it with the neighbouring slab and buttress for a fuller day in the canyon.

ca_o_schoolhouse_rock.blurb: A short sector at the far right end of the West Face at Riverside Quarry, in Riverside. It is the gentle corner of the quarry: fourteen sport routes and one top-rope, mostly 50 to 60 feet and more slabby and softer in feel than the rest of the granite. Grades are mainly 5.6 to 5.9, with a few at 5.10 and one easy line, so it suits newer sport climbers and anyone teaching lead skills. A standard rack of quickdraws is all you need, and you can walk or downclimb off instead of rappelling. Slips on the slabs can mean a long slide, and the broken rock at the start of the approach needs care.

ca_main_rock_3.blurb: The big, steep rock that anchors the Grizzly Peak Boulders in the Berkeley Hills, in the East Bay. Fifteen boulder problems tackle a tall overhanging face, with almost all of them hard: a few easy ones, then a long run from V5 up to V8. Landings are mostly flat dirt, so bring pads, and the top-outs ask for committing moves onto less steep ground around twelve feet up. The area sits high on the ridge and is often in fog, though the face looks southwest and gets sun on clear days. Walk off the back by an easy short downclimb.
